teaching_point: Scrofuloderma: firm, painless, dusky-red cold nodule over the neck overlying a matted node — exactly the Case 1 picture (painless neck lesions + matted non-tender cervical nodes + pulmonary TB).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scrofuloderma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-tuberculosis

teaching_point: Scrofuloderma in a child: nodules break down into undermined ulcers/sinuses that discharge caseous material near the angle of the jaw/ear (overlying infected nodes).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scrofuloderma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-tuberculosis

teaching_point: Later scrofuloderma: linear sinus tracts and cord-like puckered scars along the neck — healing is slow and leaves characteristic scarring.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scrofuloderma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-tuberculosis

teaching_point: Lupus vulgaris (good immunity, paucibacillary): slowly enlarging red-brown plaque on head/neck; "apple-jelly" nodules on diascopy. Long-standing lesions can develop SCC.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lupus vulgaris (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-tuberculosis

teaching_point: Tuberculosis verrucosa cutis (warty TB): exogenous re-inoculation in a previously sensitised host; warty plaque on hands/knees/buttocks.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cutaneous tuberculosis/warty tuberculosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-tuberculosis

teaching_point: Acute miliary (disseminated) cutaneous TB: crops of tiny papules/pustules — haematogenous spread in poor immunity (e.g. HIV, infants); systemically unwell → emergency.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cutaneous miliary tuberculosis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-tuberculosis

teaching_point: Tuberculid: erythema induratum of Bazin — tender violaceous nodules on the posterior calves that may ulcerate; hypersensitivity to TB elsewhere (no organisms seen in lesion).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Cutaneous tuberculosis: Bazin disease (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tuberculids

teaching_point: Papulonecrotic tuberculid: symmetrical crops of necrotic-centred papules on extensor limbs, healing with varioliform scars — answer to the tutor question "what are tuberculids?".
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Papulonecrotic tuberculid (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/tuberculids

teaching_point: Strongly positive (blistering) Mantoux/tuberculin reaction — marks high delayed-type hypersensitivity, as seen with lupus vulgaris and tuberculids; does not by itself distinguish active from latent TB.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Mantoux test reaction (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-tuberculosis

teaching_point: Thoracic zoster: grouped vesicles on red base in a band-like unilateral dermatome stopping at the midline — the commonest site; Case 2 was T9–T10 on the back.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes zoster (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-zoster

teaching_point: Unilateral dermatomal clusters across the back/shoulder — sharply respects the midline. Severe pain/burning often precedes the rash by days (prodrome).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes zoster (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-zoster

teaching_point: Grouped, partly haemorrhagic/crusting vesicles along a dermatome — haemorrhagic, necrotic or multi-dermatome disease should raise suspicion of immunosuppression (e.g. HIV).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes Zoster (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-zoster

teaching_point: Close-up of confluent vesicles on erythematous base — swab vesicle fluid for VZV PCR if diagnosis uncertain or atypical/immunocompromised.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Shingles (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-zoster

teaching_point: Severe, necrotic V1 (ophthalmic) zoster — same-day ophthalmology. Tutor pearl: Hutchinson's sign (tip/side of nose involved → nasociliary branch → high risk of eye involvement).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes zoster (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-zoster

teaching_point: Forehead/scalp V1 zoster with crusting near the eye — check for red eye, visual change, photophobia; refer urgently (HZO).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes zoster (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-zoster

teaching_point: Herald ("mother") patch: solitary 2–5 cm oval salmon-pink patch with fine inner collarette of scale — Case 3 "Picture 1". Easily mistaken for tinea corporis (do skin scrapings if unsure).
dermnet_caption: The herald patch of pityriasis rosea
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — The herald patch of pityriasis rosea (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pityriasis-rosea-images

condition: pityriasis rosea and a herald patch on the torso
teaching_point: Herald patch with the later secondary eruption of smaller ovals — Case 3 "Picture 2" (rash ~2 weeks after the first patch, post-URTI).
dermnet_caption: Pityriasis rosea and a herald patch on the torso
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pityriasis rosea and a herald patch on the torso (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pityriasis-rosea-images

condition: oval lesions orientated along the ribs
teaching_point: Long axes of the ovals follow skin cleavage (Langer) lines along the ribs — the "Christmas-tree" pattern on the back.
dermnet_caption: Oval annular lesions of pityriasis rosea with the long axis of the oval orientated around the ribs
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Oval annular lesions of pityriasis rosea with the long axis of the oval orientated around the ribs (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pityriasis-rosea-images

condition: annular collaretted lesions in truncal pityriasis rosea
teaching_point: Trailing collarette of scale just inside the edge — contrasts with tinea (scale at the advancing edge) and guttate psoriasis (thicker silvery scale over the whole papule).
dermnet_caption: Annular collaretted lesions in truncal pityriasis rosea
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Annular collaretted lesions in truncal pityriasis rosea (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pityriasis-rosea-images

condition: pityriasis rosea and a herald patch in skin of colour
teaching_point: Skin of colour: lesions look grey-brown/violaceous rather than pink, and papular/inverse forms are more frequent; post-inflammatory pigment change can persist for months.
dermnet_caption: Pityriasis rosea and a herald patch in skin of colour
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pityriasis rosea and a herald patch in skin of colour (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pityriasis-rosea-images

teaching_point: Widespread truncal secondary eruption sparing face, palms and soles — involvement of palms/soles should prompt syphilis serology.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pityriasis rosea on the back (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/pityriasis-rosea-images

teaching_point: DDx: guttate psoriasis — many small (<1 cm) "rain-drop" papules with silvery scale, classically 1–3 weeks after streptococcal sore throat; no herald patch.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Close up of guttate psoriasis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/guttate-psoriasis

teaching_point: DDx: guttate psoriasis on the back — compare the uniform drop-like papules with the oval, cleavage-line-aligned PR plaques in W5C03.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Guttate psoriasis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/guttate-psoriasis

teaching_point: DDx (raised by tutor): secondary syphilis — copper-coloured papules on palms/soles; papules tender to blunt pressure (Buschke–Ollendorff sign). PR-like rash + palms/soles or sexual risk → test/GUM.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Secondary syphilis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/syphilis

teaching_point: Recurrent herpes labialis: small grouped vesicles on the vermilion border/lip, preceded by tingling — Case 4 ("fever" + similar lesions several times before = "fever blisters/cold sores").
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes simplex labialis (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/herpes-simplex-images

teaching_point: Crusting stage of a cold sore extending onto the skin above the lip; heals without scarring in ~7–10 days. Same site each time (latent in trigeminal ganglion).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes simplex labialis (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/herpes-simplex-images

teaching_point: Herpes labialis in skin of colour — erythema less obvious; look for grouped vesicles/erosions and crust with darker post-inflammatory change.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes labialis (© Dr Mashihul Hossain) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-simplex

teaching_point: Recurrent HSV can occur at any facial site (cheek) — always in the same place; a localised recurrent vesicular cluster should not be confused with zoster (dermatomal, usually once).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes simplex on the cheek (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-simplex

teaching_point: Red flag: extensive, persistent ulcerating HSV of the lips in HIV — chronic (>4 weeks) or atypical HSV in immunosuppression needs specialist/systemic antivirals.
dermnet_caption: Extenive lip erosions due to chronic herpes simplex infection in HIV
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Extenive lip erosions due to chronic herpes simplex infection in HIV (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/herpes-simplex-images

teaching_point: Emergency: eczema herpeticum — monomorphic punched-out erosions/vesicles spreading over eczematous skin, often unwell/febrile → same-day assessment (NICE: urgent oral/IV aciclovir).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Eczema herpeticum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/eczema-herpeticum

teaching_point: Herpetic whitlow: painful vesicles/swelling of fingertip (children who suck thumbs; healthcare workers) — do NOT incise; can mimic paronychia.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpetic whitlow (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/herpes-simplex

condition: herpes simplex labialis associated with erythema multiforme
teaching_point: Recurrent HSV is the commonest trigger of erythema multiforme (target lesions, lip involvement) — a reason to consider suppressive aciclovir.
dermnet_caption: Herpes simplex labialis associated with erythema multiforme
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Herpes simplex labialis associated with erythema multiforme (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/herpes-simplex-images

teaching_point: Scarlet fever face: flushed cheeks with relative pallor around the mouth (circumoral pallor) in a febrile child with sore throat.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scarlet fever (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scarlet-fever

teaching_point: Fine punctate "sandpaper" erythema on the trunk, typically starting 12–48 h after fever/sore throat on neck/chest and spreading — feel the roughness.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scarlet fever (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scarlet-fever

teaching_point: Diffuse blanching punctate erythema on the limbs; check flexures (antecubital fossa/axillae) for linear accentuation (Pastia lines).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scarlet fever (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scarlet-fever

teaching_point: Widespread toxin-mediated erythema with accentuation in skin creases — distinguish from toxic shock syndrome (hypotension, multi-organ) and Kawasaki disease (≥5 days fever, conjunctivitis).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scarlet fever (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scarlet-fever

teaching_point: Facial scarlet fever in a child (DermNet caption: scarlet fever). Our reading: perinasal crusting suggests a concurrent impetigo/skin source of group A strep — GAS can enter via skin as well as throat.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Scarlet fever (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scarlet-fever

teaching_point: Convalescent desquamation of fingers/toes ~1–2 weeks after onset — supportive retrospective sign (also seen after Kawasaki disease and TSS).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Peeling toes after scarlet fever (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/scarlet-fever

teaching_point: Early "white strawberry tongue": white coat with red, swollen fungiform papillae poking through, plus pharyngitis and palatal petechiae (Forchheimer spots) in confirmed GAS infection (days 1–2).
dermnet_caption: (Wikimedia Commons, not DermNet) Strep throat with white strawberry tongue
licence_note: CC BY-SA 4.0 — attribution and share-alike required; DermNet has no strawberry-tongue image on its public scarlet fever page
attribution: Image: Strep throat with white strawberry tongue by Whispyhistory, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons — https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Strep_throat_with_white_strawberry_tongue.jpg

teaching_point: Later "red strawberry / raspberry tongue": white coat sheds leaving a beefy red tongue with prominent papillae (around day 4–5). Strawberry tongue also occurs in Kawasaki disease and toxic shock syndrome (tutor point).
dermnet_caption: (Wikimedia Commons, not DermNet) Scharlach (raspberry tongue, later stage of scarlet fever)
